messages.content: Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

**Year in Review: Engineering**

This year we shipped fewer features than last year, and we're calling that a win. The team spent the first two quarters paying down debt in the payments pipeline instead of adding to it. It was slow, unglamorous work — rewriting retry logic, killing three cron jobs nobody remembered starting, and cutting our on-call pages by half. Nobody wrote a blog post about it at the time. This is that post.

The second half looked different. Once the pipeline stopped catching fire, we built the things people had been asking for since last January: real-time inventory sync, the export tool finance has wanted for two years, and a new onboarding flow that cut setup time from twenty minutes to four. None of that would have landed on the old foundation.

We also changed how we work. Code review moved from a bottleneck to a same-day expectation, mostly because we agreed to review in smaller chunks. Incident retros stopped being blame sessions and started producing actual follow-up tickets that got closed.

None of this was smooth. We missed a deadline on the export tool by six weeks because we underestimated the migration. We had one bad outage in March that cost us a weekend. Both taught us something we needed to know.

We're carrying two things into next year: more of the boring reliability work, because it kept paying off, and a real push on the search rewrite we keep deferring.

Thanks to everyone who did the unglamorous parts. That's most of the job.
